findings.interpretation: On this Apple ARM64/NumPy 2.2.5 Accelerate build, even a finite 100x16 all-ones product emits divide-by-zero, overflow, and invalid RuntimeWarnings while returning exact finite 16s. The flags are set by the matmul call itself after the exception flags are cleared. The source175 operations likewise have finite operands/results and match independent scalar math.fsum reductions to roundoff. This identifies a backend warning/FP-flag artifact for these observed products, not a nonfinite result or solver convergence; it does not validate the experimental preconditioner.
findings.no_warning_suppression: Warnings remain recorded in this audit and the original exploratory output. No np.errstate or warnings filter change was made.
findings.warning_location: cardboard_offline_conditioning_study.py:409, Z[:, :j+1] @ y in the offline GMRES iterate reconstruction

warning_messages: divide by zero encountered in matmul

limits: GMRES remains exploratory CPU code, not production Matter FGMRES.
The source capture is a rejected root3/Newton23 state; not an accepted physical solution.
The fsum comparison covers only the small Z@y accumulation. It does not validate the LAPACK least-squares solve, sparse A, patch factors, or native RAP.
The fenv flag probe and warning behavior are specific to this Python/NumPy/Accelerate build and should not be generalized to other BLAS backends.
